vocabulary.definition: the action or state of setting someone or something apart from other people or things
vocabulary.example: The policy of segregation in South Africa deprived the Black majority of quality education and job opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: to move to a new place or position
vocabulary.example: Under Apartheid, millions of Africans were forcibly relocated back to the reserves.

vocabulary.definition: to rid (someone or something) of an unwanted quality, condition, or feeling
vocabulary.example: The government purged the non-white population from the voters' roll during the Apartheid era.

vocabulary.definition: to cause (someone) to adopt radical positions on political or social issues
vocabulary.example: The events of the Apartheid period radicalized many anti-Apartheid leaders.

vocabulary.definition: an official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular country
vocabulary.example: Some countries enacted trade embargoes against South Africa in response to Apartheid policies.

vocabulary.definition: marking the beginning of an institution, activity, or period of office
vocabulary.example: In the nation's inaugural all-inclusive elections, Mandela became South Africa's first Black president.
